subject: Materials Science
title: Erosion-Corrosion: Flowing Destruction
description: A quick win: understand Erosion-Corrosion: Flowing Destruction.

hook.text: A copper elbow in a hot water pipe thins and bursts in years — the bend accelerates corrosion with flow.

buildup.text: Erosion-corrosion combines mechanical wear from flow with electrochemical dissolution — worse than either alone.

discovery.text: Fast-flowing fluid strips protective oxide films — exposing fresh metal that corrodes immediately.

twist.text: Elbows, tees, and restrictions get the worst attack — anywhere flow accelerates or becomes turbulent.

climax.text: Power plant condensers use titanium tubes because it resists erosion-corrosion from cooling water.

punchline.text: Flowing water doesn't just corrode — it scrubs away the armor too.

quiz.question: Where is erosion-corrosion most severe in piping?
options: At elbows, tees, and flow restrictions where velocity increases
At the lowest point where water pools
